data.generation: Euler-Maruyama at dt_fine = 0.01 for the Day 9 ground-truth McKean-Vlasov SDE (see ground_truth_sde). Observations every 0.05 on [0, 6] (121 points per particle). Each sample is an ENSEMBLE of 64 interacting particles; the mean-field input m_t is the ensemble's empirical mean at time t, computed from the observed particles.
data.initial_law: Per ensemble, m0 ~ Uniform(-1.2, 1.2); per particle X(0) ~ Normal(m0, 0.6^2), independent given m0. Many initial means, never one (Day 5 reflection).

degrees.drift_factorized_free: powers {(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(0,1),(1,1)} in (x, m), standard train mean/scale
degrees.drift_factorized_origin: powers {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(0,1),(1,1)} in (x, m), mean-0 standardization (scale only), so the expanded polynomial genuinely vanishes at (x, m) = (0, 0), the structural constraint for the truth drift

distillation.library_variables: All libraries are polynomials in (x, m): the particle state x and the ensemble mean m at the same time. The truth drift is f(x, m) = 0.1 x - x^3 + 0.9 m, so the factorized libraries are the structural candidates (Day 7 lesson: structural libraries are included, and their win/loss is read as a diagnostic of the teacher's structure satisfaction).
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed (x, m_t) pairs of each split (ensemble-disjoint train/validation/test: splitting by ensemble, never by particle within an ensemble, because particles in one ensemble share m_t); teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.drift: f(x, m) = (x - x^3) + 0.9 * (m - x) = 0.1 x - x^3 + 0.9 m, where m = E[X_t] is the law's mean (mean-field term). This is the paper's form (2): an Ito drift f(x) plus a mean-field term E[phi(x, y)] with attraction phi(x, y) = -(x - y) (Figure 1b), with theta = 0.9.
ground_truth_sde.form: McKean-Vlasov SDE dX_t = f(X_t, m_t) dt + 0.6 dW_t with m_t = E[X_t], realized as a finite interacting-particle system (64 particles per ensemble, empirical mean as m_t). The paper's diffusion is a known constant sigma in its analysis (Section 2.1), matching the constant-g cut here.

H2_diffusion_distillation.note: Headline is the g NRMSE; the Sigma clause is the identified-object clause (Sigma = g^2 in 1D). Both must hold.

H3_truth_recovery.note: Field-level clauses only; the coefficient clause H3c is separate (Day 1 lesson).

H3c_mean_field_coefficients.diagnostic_fit: Pre-frozen diagnostic fit, NOT the selected model: factorized-free library (powers {(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(0,1),(1,1)}, threshold 0.05) fitted on train queries to the teacher, expanded to original coordinates. Compared quantities: the expanded linear x coefficient (truth 0.1) and the expanded m coefficient (truth 0.9, the interaction strength).
H3c_mean_field_coefficients.note: The (x, m) collinearity gate is the degree-3 full-library VIF (maximum selectable degree, constant column excluded, Day 8 lesson). If the maximum VIF exceeds 10, the coefficient split is reported as collinearity-limited and H3c is read as indeterminate rather than as a pass/fail on the coefficients; the frozen thresholds above still apply to the diagnostic fit's point estimates and are reported either way.

H4_simulation.domain_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated particles whose |X| ever exceeds 8.0 at any simulated step; a domain-validity measure separate from failure (Day 4 reflection).
H4_simulation.mean_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated ensembles whose |m_t| ever exceeds 5.0; the mean-field-specific domain measure.
H4_simulation.note: Paired RMSE is the per-particle per-step absolute distance between symbolic and teacher simulated states, median over test particles and steps; the threshold is loose (1.0) because mean-field feedback amplifies small drift differences, so it is NOT the main simulation clause -- failure, excursion and mean-excursion rates carry the verdict. Failure is non-finite state or |X| > 30. Each model computes its own ensemble mean from its own simulated particles at every step (self-consistent mean field).

nll_clause.note: Test-transition predictive NLL per transition: MV teacher (input (x, m)) versus Ito teacher (input x only). Clause: NLL(Ito) - NLL(MV) > 0.02 nats and > 2 x paired SE of per-transition NLL differences. Absolute NLL levels for both teachers are reported alongside (Day 7 reflection: absolute levels, not only a difference).

phase_clause.note: MAIN clause is absolute levels, pre-decided (Day 7 reflection): on the subset of test ensembles with |m0| >= 0.8 (initial ensemble mean), the mean over the subset of |m_T| at T = 6 must be within 0.15 of the truth's value for both the MV teacher and the symbolic model. The Ito teacher's separation is judged by a RELATIVE ratio (Day 8 reflection: for a level-like quantity, a ratio, not an absolute difference, is the main clause): Ito mean |m_T| / truth mean |m_T| <= 0.80. The subset size is reported; if it is below 4 ensembles the phase clause is reported as indeterminate.

H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.coarsening: MV EM teacher retrained on observations subsampled to Delta t = 0.5 (every 10th observation) with m frozen at the step start (the mean-field-specific approximation structure, declared here) vs MV EM teacher trained on the same number of transitions subsampled from Delta t = 0.05 data (transition-count-matched, Day 6 lesson).
H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.note: Day 1 reflection adapted to MV-SDEs, with Day 6/7 regime lessons: the hypothesis is regime-split by |m| (small |m| < 0.3 vs large |m| > 0.8, the regimes where the frozen-m approximation differs), and per-transition SNR is quantified (|f| dt against g sqrt(dt), by regime, using truth f and g) alongside transition-count matching. Drift and diffusion coarse-vs-fine comparisons are interpreted separately. A linear-vs-nonlinear diagnostic is reported separately: the main teacher's drift error vs truth split by |x| regime (near-linear |x| < 0.5 vs cubic-dominated |x| > 1.5).

H7_downstream_one_step.note: |MSE_symbolic - MSE_teacher| for one-step-ahead mean predictions on test transitions, where the predicted mean is x + f(x, m) dt and the target is the realized next state. Paired SE reported; if paired SE >= 0.001 (half the threshold) the clause is reported as 'not statistically established' even if the point estimate passes (Day 4 reflection).

paper.authors: Haoming Yang, Ali Hasan, Yuting Ng, Vahid Tarokh
paper.experiment: Sections 2-3: MV-SDE dX_t = f(X_t, t) dt + E_{y ~ p_t}[phi(X_t, y)] dt + sigma dW_t, with attraction phi(x, y) = -(x - y) (Figure 1b double-well phase transition); empirical-measure (EM), implicit-measure (IM) and marginal-law (ML) architectures for representing the distributional dependence, with maximum-likelihood estimators. Empirical comparisons on synthetic and real time-series and probabilistic-modeling data.
paper.title: Neural McKean-Vlasov Processes: Distributional Dependence in Diffusion Processes

reflections_applied.day1_collinearity_gate_at_max_degree: VIF is computed on train queries for the degree-3 full (x, m) library (the maximum degree the selection procedure can choose), with the constant column excluded (Day 8 lesson: its VIF is a spurious 1e9). H3c uses a pre-frozen factorized diagnostic fit as the verdict vehicle (Day 7 lesson: the gate is placed on the maximum selectable degree, and a coefficient verdict on the selected model is not taken directly).
reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: H6 is the adapted discretization-bias diagnostic: MV EM at Delta t = 0.5 (m frozen at step start, declared approximation structure) vs transition-count-matched Delta t = 0.05, regime-split by |m|, with per-transition SNR quantified by regime and drift/diffusion interpreted separately. A linear-vs-nonlinear regime split of the main teacher's drift error (|x| < 0.5 vs |x| > 1.5) is the Day 1 linear/nonlinear comparison analogue.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold diagnostic is standard: a fixed (x, m) grid, x in [-3, 3] and m in [-1.5, 1.5] (91 points), for f and g, reported on field / off-manifold axes separately and used for reporting only, never for selection (Day 5). Grid points with |m| beyond the observed m range carry no strong extrapolation claim (Day 3); in-range vs out-of-range m slices are reported separately.
reflections_applied.day4_domain_validity: H4 carries domain clauses separate from failure: particle excursion (|X| > 8) and the mean-field-specific ensemble-mean excursion (|m_t| > 5).
reflections_applied.day4_downstream_paired_se: H5 NLL clause and H7 report paired SEs with pre-frozen indeterminate rules.
reflections_applied.day5_distribution_vs_field: No distribution-matching teacher is used (all teachers are transition-likelihood Gaussian EM), so no distribution-loss verdict can be confused with a field verdict; teacher-vs-truth and symbolic-vs-teacher errors are tabulated side by side, and H5 reports absolute NLL levels for both teachers.
reflections_applied.day5_multiple_initial_conditions: Every ensemble has its own initial mean m0 ~ Uniform(-1.2, 1.2) and its particles have independent Normal(m0, 0.6^2) initial states (no single initial condition).
reflections_applied.day5_off_manifold_denominator: Grid NRMSE values above 1 are reported with absolute RMS errors alongside.
reflections_applied.day6_diffusion_input_design: Diffusion is fitted and verified separately from drift (its own full (x, m) library and verdict); a grid slice of teacher g across m at fixed x is reported to check for spurious m dependence of g (true g is constant). No trajectory-constant input exists (m varies within every ensemble over time), so the Day 6 trajectory-constant failure mode cannot arise here.
reflections_applied.day7_absolute_levels_for_shift: H5's phase clause is pre-decided as absolute levels (mean |m_T| for each model on the |m0| >= 0.8 subset), not only a degradation/difference; the Ito separation uses a relative ratio per the Day 8 rate lesson.
reflections_applied.day7_rare_domain_events: Mean-field domain events (|m_t| > 5) are tested over all simulated steps and ensembles, not by counting rare on-manifold occurrences.
reflections_applied.day7_structural_library: Drift candidates include factorized libraries and a factorized-origin library (mean-0 standardization, no constant term, so the expanded polynomial genuinely vanishes at (x, m) = (0, 0)); the teacher's structure satisfaction (its f(0, 0) value) is measured before interpreting the structural library's win/loss (Day 8 lesson).
reflections_applied.day8_meanfield_analogue_of_jump_processi: Ignoring the distributional input is the MV analogue of Day 8's jump-ignoring estimator: the Ito teacher (x only) is trained and compared against the MV teacher, so the bias from dropping m is measured directly (drift contamination) rather than assumed.
reflections_applied.day8_relative_ratios_for_levels: The Ito separation in H5's phase clause is a relative ratio (Ito mean |m_T| / truth mean |m_T| <= 0.80), not an absolute difference, following the Day 8 lesson that absolute thresholds mislead when the level itself is the quantity of interest.
reflections_applied.day8_vif_constant_excluded: VIF computation excludes the constant column (Day 8 lesson: its VIF is a spurious 1e9 from the regression intercept).

simulation.initial_states: test ensembles' initial particle states X(0) (24 ensembles x 64 particles)
simulation.self_consistent_mean: each model computes its own ensemble mean from its own simulated particles at every step

split.unit: ensemble (disjoint; particles within an ensemble are never split across splits because they share m_t)

teacher.architecture: MV teacher: two small MLPs on standardized (x, m): f net [32, 32] tanh; g net [16] tanh, output softplus + 0.01. Ito teacher (paper-axis baseline): same nets on standardized x only. All teachers trained by Adam on train transitions only. This is the paper's empirical-measure (EM) architecture analogue: the distributional input is the observed empirical mean m_t.
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Three declared cuts. (1) Latent/generative architectures (implicit-measure and marginal-law) and the paper's real time-series and probabilistic-modeling benchmarks are not treated; the teacher is reconstructed in identifiable coordinates as an observable finite-particle MV-SDE whose distributional input is the empirical ensemble mean. (2) The interaction is the paper's Figure 1b attraction phi(x, y) = -(x - y) with theta = 0.9, and the Ito drift is the double-well drift x - x^3 from the same figure; the paper's learned-measure architectures are replaced by the empirical mean input (the paper's own EM architecture analogue). (3) Training is by Gaussian transition likelihood (the series' standard estimator) rather than the paper's MV maximum-likelihood estimators; results therefore do not reproduce the paper's benchmark numbers.

em_coarse.transitions: train ensembles subsampled to every 10th observation (40 x 64 x 12 = 30720 transitions), m frozen at the step start

em_fine_sub.transitions: 30720 transitions subsampled at random (seed-fixed) from train Delta t = 0.05 transitions, matching the coarsened count

estimators_compared.ito_main: Gaussian EM on full regular train transitions, input x only -- the paper-axis baseline (distributional dependence dropped)
estimators_compared.mv_coarse: Gaussian EM on subsampled Delta t = 0.5 train transitions, input (x, m) with m frozen at step start
estimators_compared.mv_fine_sub: Gaussian EM on transition-count-matched Delta t = 0.05 train transitions, input (x, m)
estimators_compared.mv_main: Gaussian EM on full regular train transitions (dt = 0.05), input (x, m) -- the distilled teacher
